newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil -Fuel oil weak, LSWR slightly firmer.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil -Fuel oil weak, LSWR slightly firmer.

text.p: Talk was thin in the Singapore high sulphur fuel oil market on Thursday and many traders were on the sidelines searching for fresh market direction.
Traders said the market started to lose its upward momentum earlier in the week when the 180-cst grade failed to breach the previous $103.50 traded level.
The 180-cst was bid at $101.50 per tonne for mid-June delivery and offer was heard at $102.00, traders said.
"There are not many market-inspiring factors at this moment, especially after the relatively low CPC tender result," said one trader.

Taiwan's state Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it awarded a third 30,000-tonne cargo of 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil at around $100 per tonne for June 9-18 on a free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis, compared with $101.00 in its last sell tender.
News of an explosion at its Taoyuan refinery did not spark any major movements in prices, traders said.
The fuel oil swaps market was quiet, with June swaps quoted at $99.00/$100.50 against Wednesday's $99.50/$100.00 and July at $98.00/$99.25 against $98.50/$99.00.
On SIMEX fuel oil futures contract on late Thursday, June was 20 cents down to $99.80 with 15 lots traded.

Sentiment in the low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) market improved slightly after Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina announced the loading schedule for its 3.1 million barrels of LSWR for June lifting.
Although some 200,000 barrels are expected to be rolled over from May, but the total will still be far lower than that in May, boosting previous sluggish sentiment, they said.
In May, Pertamina allocated 3.85 million barrels with an additional 500,000 barrels rolled over from April.
"The price may move 40-80 cents higher in the near term," said one trader.
